header.name: Tangible User Interfaces
header.description: This course dives into the interdisciplinary field of Tangible User Interfaces (TUI) and Interaction Design. Tangible means "physical." In the broadest sense, in this course, we will understand how to experience the digital realm physically, understand different viewpoints for tangible interactions and interfaces, and find applications of such interfaces. TUIs are primarily concerned with the physical embodiment of digital information and computation and try to go beyond Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs). This course is inspired by the work of Hiroshi Ishii, Ullmer, Eva Hornecker, Michael Horn, and a few pioneers in this field, along with an India-centric context for TUIs. The course comprises hands-on activities and theoretical components with a project-based learning approach. Physical prototyping will be conducted with readily available tools in DI Lab.

A laptop/ computer that can support high end applications.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be introduced to the concept of tangible user interface and interaction design.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will understand different views of Tangible User Interfaces.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to conceptualize, design and prototype TUIs

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to critically and scientifically evaluate the user experience design of TUIs

lecture_topics: Review of past and existing works
Enabling tools and technologies for TUI.
Tools and technologies for enabling prototyping TUIs
Aesthetics of Tangible and Embodied Interactions
Cognitive, Technical and User Interaction Perspectives
